scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W285 has clear radiating wavy lines around its dark mass — the draft's chapter 1 description of it as having almost no radiating marks is incorrect; it belongs with the radiating-field works, not the 'silhouette alone' opener. Corrected by moving W285 to chapter 2 and replacing it in chapter 1 with W047, which genuinely has minimal surrounding marks relative to the others.

W047 observation notes jagged lines fanning left and upward, but the larger image confirms the figure is a bird/duck-like silhouette on a diagonal black slope against green — the draft's 'round-bodied figure' description is acceptable at this resolution but 'curved neck' is more accurate than 'round-bodied'; prose corrected to avoid overclaiming.

W010 draft description says 'zigzag lines scatter in every direction' but the anchor image shows lines radiating outward from the head/shoulders area, not from the lower body or grass strip — corrected to 'from the head and shoulders outward'.

W158 anchor image confirms the figure is a cat in a reclining/alert pose on a black shelf, with yellow-green spiral eyes and white fang marks, and radiating yellow lines across the orange field — observations are accurate; the draft's 'crouched' is acceptable.

W285 anchor image confirms the dark form is an elephant-like shape with a trunk and lavender inner contour lines, and the radiating lines are clearly present around the whole form — the draft's chapter 1 placement as a near-markless silhouette is wrong and corrected.

W093 observations note 'a large yellow square and a broad white frame' — the image confirms this is a white-framed work with a yellow interior field and a small black figure at lower right; the draft prose is accurate.

W177 is visibly the most complex work — layered paint-like marks, a large spiral eye, yellow bar forms at the bottom — the draft's description is accurate and its placement as penultimate in chapter 4 is appropriate.
W248 background is confirmed as flat color blocks with loose crossing lines; the draft's description is accurate.
W146 is a teal figure on dark grey with a jagged crown and red marks on the face — confirmed accurate.
W208 shows a side-facing head in near-total black with a thin pink-mauve contour, a small eye cluster, and red mouth mark — confirmed accurate.
W243 shows a large black rounded head on deep red with yellow outlines, concentric circle eyes, white dashed stitching, and isolated blue marks — confirmed accurate.

Transition from W037 to W285 in original chapter 1 referenced 'spiral eye replaced by white X' — this is valid but W285 also has prominent radiating lines making it a poor fit for 'silhouette alone'; corrected by restructuring.
Chapter 1 now uses W093, W037, W047 — all three have minimal or no radiating field marks relative to the rest of the set, making the chapter coherent.

Chapter 2 now includes W285, W010, W062, W179 — all have prominent radiating fields; W285's radiating lines are dark on lavender rather than yellow on warm ground, providing useful contrast within the chapter.
W047 moved to chapter 1: its jagged lines fan in one direction only and are sparse compared to the full-surround radiating fields of W010, W062, W179, W285 — an honest fit for the reduced chapter.
Repetitive use of 'charged' across multiple stops reduced.
Transition prose revised to reference both visible works specifically rather than only the preceding one.
No artist psychology, chronology, influence, or biography introduced.
No invented objects or expressions added.
All 15 slots appear exactly once.
evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study
evidence.wordingReviewScope: Text-only tightening of image-reviewed headings and invitations; no new image inspection or membership change
evidence.assistantWordingScope: Specificity and overstatement corrections to exhibition headings and invitations. Existing image-reviewed memberships, chapter order and artwork roles remain intact.
evidence.referenceExpansionMethod: Exact collection-plan slot to title and CID lookup; no new interpretation

title: Characters in Silhouette
question: How much can a solid shape tell us?
introduction: A dark shape can establish a character with only a few additional marks. Follow silhouettes across colored grounds, then compare eye shapes, mouth signs and lines around or within the body. Later works make the dark area less continuous. Notice which details alter recognition while the larger shape remains a useful landmark.
closing: Compare two silhouettes with different facial marks. What remains recognizable if you look at the larger dark shapes first?

chapters.title: The Shape Alone
chapters.introduction: Three works open with the most reduced version of the structure: one dark shape, one flat field, and almost nothing else added to either.

stops.whyHere: The smallest, most isolated figure in the exhibition: a rounded black form in a wide yellow field, its stitched grin and looped eyes the only marks that break the seal.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #62

stops.whyHere: A low black dome on teal; a single spiral eye is the sole interior mark, the wide empty field above left unbroken.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #62 sits in open yellow warmth at lower right; this shape presses to the ground on cool teal, same economy of marks, different weight and temperature.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #103

stops.whyHere: A bird-like silhouette on saturated green; jagged lines fan in one direction only, and two yellow X-eyes with a stitched mouth are the sole color on the form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #103's single spiral eye gives way to paired X-eyes here; the radiating lines shift from a full arc to a one-sided fan, keeping the field mostly open.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #112

chapters.title: Fields Filled with Lines
chapters.introduction: Four works surround the silhouette with radiating lines that extend across the field in every direction, describing the space around the figure rather than the figure itself.

stops.whyHere: A dark rounded mass on lavender, wavy lines radiating outward from its entire edge; inner lavender contour lines and a detached oval below are the only marks on the form itself.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #112's lines fan to one side on green; here dark lines radiate from all sides on a cool lavender field, and the form turns inward rather than outward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #268

stops.whyHere: A wide-armed silhouette on amber; zigzag lines scatter outward from the head and shoulders across the whole field, denser on the left, while a grass strip anchors the base.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #268's dark lines on lavender give way to black zigzags on warm amber — the radiating marks grow more agitated and the palette heats up.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #88

stops.whyHere: A one-legged figure on orange; two distinct line rhythms — tight zigzags above, slower waves below — give the surrounding space a split quality that the figure's unresolved stance echoes.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #88's lines radiate uniformly from a static form; here the lines divide into two registers around a figure whose balance is itself unresolved.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #92

stops.whyHere: A squat, stepped black shape on olive-yellow; yellow lines pulse outward in all directions while a zigzag mouth reads as snarl or grin depending on the moment.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #92's single-legged instability gives way to a wide, grounded frontality — but the all-direction radiating lines and ambiguous mouth sustain the pressure.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #60

chapters.title: The Eye Mark
chapters.introduction: Four works place the eye at the center of attention, each using a different form — loop, spiral, concentric ring — producing a different quality of looking back at the viewer.

stops.whyHere: Double-loop yellow eyes and a W-shaped mouth on a teal-grounded rabbit form; the eyes hold the gaze with an alertness that the radiating lines behind the figure amplify.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #60's zigzag mouth drew attention across the lower face; here the double-loop eyes pull focus upward and hold it, making the face the primary event.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #98

stops.whyHere: A pointed black form on teal with a single yellow spiral eye; tight zigzags near the jagged mouth and loose waves at the margins give the watchfulness a directional edge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #98's frontal double eyes become a single side-facing spiral here — the gaze narrows and points rather than stares outward.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #64

stops.whyHere: A reclining black cat on burnt-orange, its yellow-green spiral eyes wide and its white fang-points the only break in the silhouette; yellow lines vibrate across the whole field.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #64's cool teal field gives way to hot orange; the spiral eye form recurs but doubles, and white fang marks add a second point of interior detail.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #51

stops.whyHere: A large black rounded head on deep red, its concentric circle eyes and dashed seam-line giving it a wired, assembled quality; isolated blue marks float at the margins apart from the central form.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #51's orange field and radiating lines shift to deep red; the eye form moves from spiral to concentric ring, and the surrounding field gains isolated floating marks rather than a continuous radiated field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #147

chapters.title: When the Shape Opens
chapters.introduction: The final four works complicate the silhouette structure: color enters the form, surfaces accumulate marks, and the boundary between figure and field begins to break down.

stops.whyHere: A teal figure on dark grey — color fills the form rather than surrounding it; a jagged crown and two small red marks concentrate pressure on the face from inside the outline.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #147's black form on red is replaced by a colored form on dark grey — the silhouette logic inverts, and the marks move inside the outline rather than into the field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #266

stops.whyHere: A black side-profile held by a thin pink contour; a small blue-white eye cluster and a red mouth mark read as sparks against the dark mass, while zigzag lines continue down the torso.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #266's teal fill gives way to near-total black; the red marks shrink to a single mouth point, and the agitation spreads from face down through the body.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #277

stops.whyHere: A head in three-quarter view where the left side dissolves into layered color marks and a dense tangle of lines; the right eye socket holds a large white spiral that pulls the gaze inward against the surrounding density.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #277's restless lines are held within a clear outline; here the outline breaks on one side and the interior marks spill outward, collapsing the boundary between figure and field.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #70

stops.whyHere: The most layered work in the exhibition: a black mass with framed eye zones, tooth rows, and a background of flat color blocks crossed by loose lines — the silhouette strategy at its most loaded.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: nnxyz nnotb #70's partial dissolution becomes total here; the background is no longer a single flat field but a patchwork of color blocks, and the figure's features multiply into confrontational density.
stops.title: nnxyz nnotb #165
